instructions.purpose: Search stored conversation memories semantically for facts, preferences, history, or other personal information previously shared by the user.

tool.name: search-memory
tool.description: Queries the memory database for the current conversation. The chat context is handled automatically. Every call requires query as a natural-language semantic query; limit can optionally cap the number of facts returned. Semantic matches are ranked by cosine distance: a lower cosine distance means a closer semantic match. An empty result means the requested information is unsupported by stored memory.

instructions.response_handling: Use only facts explicitly present in the returned facts array. An empty facts array means the requested information is unsupported: report that it is unknown or not found. Never fill gaps by guessing, inferring, or treating the query itself as evidence.

arguments.query: Required. A short natural-language phrase naming ONE thing to recall, ideally under ten words and never over 120 characters. Not keywords, not a partial-text pattern, and not several topics at once.
arguments.limit: Optional. Caps the number of returned facts; prefer 5-10 and never exceed 25.

usage_rules.rule: Always provide query as a specific natural-language semantic query
Describe the meaning of the information sought instead of copying isolated keywords
Keep the query short and about a single topic; a long query listing several topics matches nothing because it lands between all of them
When you need several unrelated things, call the tool once per thing rather than combining them into one query
Use limit to avoid overwhelming context with too many results (prefer 5-10)
Prefer facts from results with lower distance because lower cosine distance means they are semantically closer
Do not claim that memory supports a fact unless a returned fact explicitly contains it
If the facts array is empty, treat the requested fact as unsupported and do not guess

example.context: W pełni fikcyjny przykład po polsku. Użytkownik pyta: "Co pamiętasz o moim rowerze o imieniu Kometa?"

toolCall.query: Jakie informacje użytkownik wcześniej podał o swoim rowerze o imieniu Kometa?

example.reasoning: The query is a complete natural-language description. Both facts may be used because they are explicitly returned, and 0.08 is closer than 0.19 because lower cosine distance means greater semantic similarity.

example.context: Fully fictional English-to-Polish example. The user asks in English: "Does my bicycle named Kometa have a basket?"

toolCall.query: Czy rower użytkownika o imieniu Kometa ma koszyk?

example.reasoning: The English request is expressed as a natural-language semantic query in Polish. The empty result does not support either yes or no, so the answer must say that memory does not establish whether Kometa has a basket.
